$notes: The foley bus (review round 2): sparse practical sounds, at most 10 in the film, each in a speech gap or under a line's last words. Synthesized by generator/film/lib/foley.mjs; mixed by film:mix after the master gain, dry plus a small-room reverb, at lufsS (max short-term LUFS, -28 to -32). Anchors are shot-local, so each event follows its shot's re-fit. A shot that moves one of these moments must move the anchor here too.

events.why: The case opens: the study lamp clicks on (bookends fx-lamp-off at the end of the film). In the gap before L0106.

Review round 4: the first of the film's three STATUS: OPEN stamps (the fence question card, ON 'stands' in L1418; beat ch14-s07 stamp = T.word(L1418, stands)). The quietest and driest of the three (-32 LUFS S, room 16 dB under the hit, cut to 0.6 s) so it never masks 'stands'; underWord allows the onset under that one word only.

Review round 4: the second STATUS: OPEN stamp, on the HOW FAR? HOW FAST? card ON 'open' (the last word of L1516b; beat ch15-s08 stamp = T.word(L1516b, open)), so the clack lands under the line's last word. Between the fence stamp (-32) and the final fx-stamp (-29): a clack means the question stays open, three times.
STATUS: OPEN stamped on the case card (wordless beat after L1518). The strongest of the film's three stamps (-29; fx-stamp-fence -32, fx-stamp-howfar -31).
The desk lamp clicks off (b4), in the gap before L1520.
The match strikes on 'new' (round-2 ch15-s09 note): the scratch starts on the word and its ignition pop lands on 'candles', where the flare and the wick take over.
The flare as the wick catches on 'candles', settling by 'from'.
